description.purpose: Deterministic screening on an ingress channel, as topology: one code cell and one rule store between the surface and the agent, plus a transfer lane and the custody of a parked turn. Every inbound turn is measured -- size, sender, forbidden literal, rate -- against one normalised form (NFKC, whitespace collapsed, casefolded) on both sides of every comparison, and ENDS on exactly one of two lanes: 'pass' with the body byte-identical, or 'reject' naming the reason AND the rule that fired. Since 2.2.0 a third verdict 'hold' ends nothing: the turn is parked whole until a person releases or refuses it, or its timeout runs out -- and then it ends on one of the same two lanes (GH #450). Above every row stands the HARDLINE: a layer that is code rather than rows, consulted first, able to say only reject, and unreachable by any update an operator or an attacker could write (GH #449). Nothing here asks a model, and nothing here can: every verdict is a comparison or a clock. The rule set lives in rows, so a colony shows its screening policy as part of its tree and changes it with an insert.
description.use_when: In front of every inbound channel -- Telegram, Slack, HTTP, voice -- wherever a stranger can reach the surface. Instantiate it in the SAME mutation that wires the ingress lane and both exits: the surface into ./screen with hop.route 'in_turn' and the channel identity promoted to context.channel (and context.user_id where the surface has one), ./screen out on hop.route=='pass' into the agent's intake, and ./screen out on hop.route=='reject' into a drain or a log. Both exit edges MUST delete the firewall's context keys (fw_body, fw_now, fw_phase, store_origin), otherwise the parked copy of the turn rides along downstream. Since 2.2.0 the hive also carries the HOLD lanes -- `in_release` (one person's answer about one parked turn) and `in_sweep` (expire what is due) in, `hold` (the notice, carrying the turn itself) out. All three are OPT-IN: a colony with no enabled 'hold' row never uses them, and `params.required_drains` asks about them only if an edge names them -- so a parent that wired only `in_turn` is untouched. Since 2.1.0 the hive also carries a TRANSFER lane: `in_export` hands the rule table out as a versioned document and `in_import` takes one back into a running hive. Wire both drains (`dump` and `reject`) in the same mutation as the ingress -- `params.required_drains` refuses it otherwise (GH #471).
description.not_in_scope: No answer to the sender: the firewall never speaks outbound, and what a reject becomes -- a drain, a log line, a polite refusal, a ban -- is the parent tree's decision. It does not notify anyone about a held turn either: it emits the notice, and who reads it is the parent's. No model judgement of any kind, not for classification and not for phrasing. No regex an operator can write: a pattern rule is a normalised substring, prefix, suffix or fnmatch glob. No precedence beyond hardline > deny > allow > hold -- first match per class decides, specificity does not matter, and an allow exception cannot be carved out of a broad deny. The hardline layer has no grant path at all: it can refuse and nothing else, because a layer that could allow would be an authority mechanism. No secret handling, no auth, no session: the firewall knows a channel and a user id, nothing about who they are. No clock of its own: a hold's timeout is measured whenever custody is touched, so `in_sweep` wants a timer in the parent if the receipt has to be punctual. No pruning of the arrivals ledger and no deletion of a rule -- disabling a row is the retraction. And neither the arrivals ledger nor the hold pile travels in an export: the rate window is the budget THIS installation spent, and a parked turn is a live conversation waiting on a person in a colony that no longer exists.
examples: PORTS - every endpoint is the HIVE path (`params.ports` is empty since GH #228; an edge naming ./screen is refused with hive_port_boundary). Entry: the parent edge names the lane with set_hop route 'in_turn' and promotes the identity to context.channel / context.user_id; optionally hop.recorded_at stamps the turn from outside. Exits (on hop.route, both leaving the hive path, both clearing the firewall's own context keys inside): 'pass' -> the agent's intake, body unchanged; 'reject' -> a drain or log sink, carrying hop.reject_reason and hop.rule_id.

RULE ORDER, first match decides: (H) the HARDLINE, which is not a row -- an absolute body ceiling of 262144 characters that FIREWALL_MAX_CHARS cannot be set above, and the invisible / direction-overriding codepoints that defeat every pattern row at once (ZWJ, ZWNJ and the directional marks are excluded on purpose, so emoji and right-to-left text pass); (1) size cap FIREWALL_MAX_CHARS, arithmetic, before the first store hop; (2) an unreadable rule row -- SKIPPED, never fatal: the row leaves the rule set, a bodiless receipt on the reject lane names it (reason 'rule_unreadable', hop.rule_fault the cause) and the turn walks on (GH #506); (3) sender blocklist; (4) sender allowlist, per dimension, an empty allowlist admits everything; (5) pattern blocklist -- substring, prefix, suffix, glob, over the NORMALISED text on both sides; (6) rate limit LAST of the refusing rules, because it is the only one that consumes budget; (7) hold LAST OF ALL, because it is the only verdict that does not end the turn.

RULE VOCABULARY -- the `rules` table has seven columns and THREE of them are CLOSED VALUE SETS the screen enforces, which `seed_rows` cannot check for you (it checks columns, never values -- GH #456/#506). `kind`: sender | substring | prefix | suffix | glob. `field`: channel | user_id | match for a `sender` row, and exactly `text` for a pattern row (substring/prefix/suffix/glob). `action`: allow | reject | hold on a `sender` row, reject | hold on a pattern row -- a pattern row can never allow. `value` is the literal (a sender value, the pattern, or -- with field `match` -- a JSON object over channel/user_id), `enabled` is 0/1 and `note` is free text the screen never reads. There is no `pattern`, no `body`, no `deny` and no regex: a row outside this vocabulary is dropped with a `rule_unreadable` receipt and enforces nothing. A worked declaration: {"seed_rows": [{"target": "./firewall/rules", "table": "rules", "rows": [ {"rule_id": "deny-phone", "kind": "glob", "field": "text", "value": "*+49*", "action": "reject", "enabled": 1, "note": "phone numbers"}, {"rule_id": "hold-money", "kind": "substring", "field": "text", "value": "invoice", "action": "hold", "enabled": 1, "note": "a person decides"} ]}]}

a fresh instance with the shipped seed: one live rule (a normalised substring on the canonical prompt-injection opener -- it refuses, it never grants, and no ordinary turn contains it) plus 8 example rows with enabled 0. The template does not ship as an open gate, and it does not brick the tree it is dropped into either; the two arithmetic rules (size, rate) are live from the first turn as they always were, and the hardline layer is live because it is not a row

closing a channel to everyone but one caller: two inserts into rules (kind sender, action allow, field channel / field user_id) and the next turn is already screened against them -- no restart, no code change. One insert does it too: a single row with field 'match' and a JSON object in value requires the user AND the channel together, which two rows cannot express because two rows are an OR

a blocked pattern demonstrably never reaches the agent: the reject lane leaves ./screen, the pass lane is the ONLY edge into the intake, and the rejected turn is on the hop with the rule_id that fired

carrying a screening policy to a second colony: `in_export` produces ONE part, drained into the member's export sink as `firewall/seed/rules.jsonl`. Birth the new firewall from that file and it screens the first turn against the rules the old one ended with, `enabled` flags included -- the arrivals ledger stays behind by design

a turn nobody has vouched for, parked for a person: one insert into rules (kind sender, field user_id, action hold) plus the three hold edges, and the next turn from that sender leaves on 'hold' instead of 'pass' -- stored whole in `held`, announced with its hold_id and its expires_at, and put back on 'pass' byte-identical when someone answers on `in_release`. Nobody answers within FIREWALL_HOLD_TTL_MS and it ends on 'reject' with 'hold_expired'; there is no third outcome and no parking bay

every row of the table disabled and a zero-width space inside the forbidden literal -> still 'reject', reason 'hardline_blocked', rule_id 'hardline:invisible-format'. No update and no delete reaches that verdict, because it is not a row -- changing it is a version bump of this template
